prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study was a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized controlled trial.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The trial included 120 patients who had chronic pain.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants received at-home transcranial electrical stimulation, either direct current aimed at the motor cortex or alternating current aimed at the prefrontal cortex.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The researchers measured pain sensitivity using quantitative sensory tests for pressure and heat thresholds, pain modulation, and temporal summation.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The effects of the stimulation were checked immediately after treatment and again after six months.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Statistical analysis showed no significant changes in the pain test scores after the stimulation at any time point.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The results do not support the idea that the pain relief from this stimulation comes from changes in how the brain modulates pain.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors suggest that future studies should check if these specific pain tests are sensitive enough to detect any changes caused by the stimulation.
facts.subject: humans
